The three turbine blades analyzed were the C3X vane, the VKI rotor, and the ACE rotor.
The C3X vane had 9 rows of film cooling holes, the VKI rotor had 6 rows, and the ACE rotor had 3 rows.
The hole diameter on all the blades was less than 1 mm.
The grid size was varied along the blade chord to maintain a ratio of 0.76 to 1.3 between adjacent grid sizes.
The C3X vane grid had 281 x 45 x 81 grid points, the VKI rotor grid had 353 x 53 x 17 grid points, and the ACE rotor grid had 313 x 53 x 17 grid points.
The y+ value for the first point off the blade surface was kept less than 1.
The computational time on the C-90 supercomputer was about 20 seconds per iteration for one million grid points.
The first case required about 1100 iterations to converge, while subsequent cases required about 300 iterations.
The incoming flow turbulence intensity was 6.5% for the C3X vane, 5.2% for the VKI rotor, and 4.0% for the ACE rotor.
The blowing ratio (Bc) ranged from 0.20 to 0.411 for the C3X vane, 0.092 to 0.352 for the VKI rotor, and 0.0 to 0.7 for the ACE rotor.
The coolant temperature ratio (Tc/T∞) ranged from 0.426 to 0.826 for the C3X vane, 0.176 to 0.352 for the VKI rotor, and 0.18 to 0.7 for the ACE rotor.
The effect of coolant distribution at the hole exit was observed to be as high as 60% on the suction surface and 50% on the pressure surface.
Mayle's transition criterion was used only for the ACE rotor, as the C3X vane and VKI rotor had turbulent flow at the leading edge due to showerhead injection.
Forest's and Crawford's models were used to account for the augmentation of heat transfer due to free-stream turbulence and film cooling, respectively.
The experimental heat transfer data was obtained using thermocouples, thin-film gages, and platinum resistance thermometers for the three blades.
